title: Light and Sound
seo_title: Grade 1 Science: Light and Sound Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Light and sound can be produced and their properties can be changed: natural and artificial sources of light and sound, and properties of light and sound (bright and dim, loud and soft, high and low). (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 1, Physics)
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 science worksheets (BC): sources of light, light and materials, how sound is made, and loud, soft, high and low sounds. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_sub: Loud or soft, high or low.
body_html:
How to think about it

The Sun, lamps and fire give light; vibrations make sound.

  • Some light comes from nature, some from people.
  • Shaking things make sound.
  • Sounds can be loud or soft, high or low.
Example

Is the Moon a source of light?

The Moon reflects sunlight.

Answer: no

Example

How can you make a drum sound louder?

Hit it harder.

Answer: hit it harder

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the Moon makes its own light.
  • Mixing up loud (volume) and high (pitch).

faq.a: Something vibrating, like a guitar string or your voice box.

faq.q: What is an artificial light source?
faq.a: A light made by people, like a flashlight or a lamp.

items.q: Which is a natural source of light?
items.e: Natural sources are not made by people.

items.q: In a room with no light at all, could you see a clock on the wall?
c: Yes, if it is shiny or white.
Yes, a little, because objects glow.
No. With no light, no light can reflect from it into your eyes.
Yes, if you wait for your eyes to get used to it.
items.e: We see objects when light reflects off them into our eyes. Dark is the absence of light.

items.q: In a room with no light at all, could you see a toy car?
c: Yes, if you wait for your eyes to get used to it.
Yes, a little, because objects glow.
No. With no light, no light can reflect from it into your eyes.
Yes, if it is shiny or white.
items.e: We see objects when light reflects off them into our eyes. Dark is the absence of light.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a light source: a cat's eye reflector on a road, a glowing computer screen, a star or a flashlight that is switched on?
c: a flashlight that is switched on
a cat's eye reflector on a road
items.e: A cat's eye reflector on a road does not make its own light; it reflects light.

items.q: Which of these is a light source: a campfire, a mirror, the Moon or the planet Venus?
items.e: A light source gives out its own light. The others only reflect light.

items.q: Which of these is a light source: a high-visibility jacket, a lit bulb, a sheet of white paper or the planet Venus?
items.e: A light source gives out its own light. The others only reflect light.

items.q: Light hits a mirror and bounces off. What is this called?
items.e: Smooth shiny surfaces reflect light well.

items.q: Which of these is a light source: a flash of lightning, a high-visibility jacket, a shiny spoon or the planet Venus?
items.e: A light source gives out its own light. The others only reflect light.

items.q: In a room with no light at all, could you see a teddy bear?
c: Yes, a little, because objects glow.
No. With no light, no light can reflect from it into your eyes.
Yes, if it is shiny or white.
Yes, if you wait for your eyes to get used to it.
items.e: We see objects when light reflects off them into our eyes. Dark is the absence of light.

items.q: Which of these is a light source: a bicycle reflector, a campfire, a shiny spoon or the planet Venus?
items.e: A light source gives out its own light. The others only reflect light.

items.q: Is a candle flame a light source?
c: not a light source: it reflects light
a light source only at night
items.e: Sources give out light; everything else is seen because it reflects light.

items.q: Which of these is a light source: a high-visibility jacket, a lit bulb, a sheet of white paper or the Moon?
items.e: A light source gives out its own light. The others only reflect light.

items.q: Which of these is a light source: a flash of lightning, a high-visibility jacket, a mirror or the Moon?
items.e: A light source gives out its own light. The others only reflect light.

c: a light source only at night
not a light source: it reflects light
items.e: Sources give out light; everything else is seen because it reflects light.

items.q: What is one danger of light?
c: Looking at the Sun can damage your eyes.
items.e: Never look straight at the Sun.

items.q: How does light travel?
items.e: That is why shadows form.

items.q: A shadow forms when …
items.e: Shadows are areas with no light.

items.q: Which material is translucent?
items.e: Translucent materials let some light through.

items.q: Is a lit bulb a light source?
c: not a light source: it reflects light
a light source only at night
items.e: Sources give out light; everything else is seen because it reflects light.

items.q: Which material is opaque?
items.e: Opaque materials block light.

items.q: Emma holds clear glass in a beam of light. What will the wall behind it look like?
items.e: Clear glass lets all the light through.

items.q: A straw in a glass of water looks bent. Why?
c: Light bends (refracts) as it passes from water to air.
items.e: This is refraction.

items.q: Is a clear swimming pool transparent, translucent or opaque?
items.e: A clear swimming pool lets almost all light through, so you can see clearly through it.

items.q: Benjamin shines a flashlight at a mirror. Where does most of the light go?
c: It goes through to the wall.
It bounces back toward the flashlight side.
items.e: A mirror is shiny. It reflects light.

items.q: Aiden holds wax paper in a beam of light. What will the wall behind it look like?
items.e: Wax paper lets some light through.

items.q: Is clean water transparent, translucent or opaque?
items.e: Clean water lets almost all light through, so you can see clearly through it.

items.q: Maya shines a flashlight at a glass of clean water. What happens to the light?
c: It lets all the light through.
items.e: A glass of clean water lets all the light through.

items.q: Which material is transparent?
items.e: Transparent materials let almost all light through.

items.q: Is a brick transparent, translucent or opaque?
items.e: A brick lets no light through and makes a dark shadow.

items.q: Is plastic wrap transparent, translucent or opaque?
items.e: Cling film lets almost all light through, so you can see clearly through it.

items.q: Owen shines a flashlight at a clear plastic cup. What happens to the light?
c: It lets all the light through.
items.e: A clear plastic cup lets all the light through.

items.q: Is wood transparent, translucent or opaque?
items.e: Wood lets no light through and makes a dark shadow.

items.q: Is greaseproof paper transparent, translucent or opaque?
items.e: Greaseproof paper lets some light through, but you cannot see clearly through it.

items.q: Noah wants to make a fish tank so you can see the fish. Which material is best?
items.e: It needs a material that lets all the light through.

items.q: Jayden shines a flashlight at a thin paper plate. What happens to the light?
c: It lets all the light through.
items.e: A thin paper plate lets some light through.

items.q: Leah wants to make a sign that shines at night when car lights hit it. Which material is best?
items.e: It needs a material that bounces the light back.

items.q: Ava shines a flashlight at a wooden block. What happens to the light?
c: It lets all the light through.
items.e: A wooden block blocks the light.

items.q: Is a clear plastic bottle transparent, translucent or opaque?
items.e: A clear plastic bottle lets almost all light through, so you can see clearly through it.

items.q: Olivia shines a flashlight at frosted glass. What happens to the light?
c: It lets all the light through.
items.e: Frosted glass lets some light through.

items.q: Is the Moon a source of light?
c: No, it reflects light from the Sun.
Yes, it makes its own light.
items.e: We see the Moon because it reflects sunlight.

items.q: Why can astronauts on the Moon not hear each other without radios?
c: There is no air to carry the sound.
items.e: Sound needs a medium.

items.q: When a loudspeaker makes a sound, what is vibrating?
c: the player's lips and the air in the tube
items.e: All sounds are made by something vibrating.

items.q: When a triangle makes a sound, what is vibrating?
c: the player's lips and the air in the tube
items.e: All sounds are made by something vibrating.

items.q: Which instrument makes a lower pitch?
items.e: Bigger instruments vibrate more slowly.

items.q: When a xylophone makes a sound, what is vibrating?
c: the player's lips and the air in the tube
items.e: All sounds are made by something vibrating.

items.q: When a guitar makes a sound, what is vibrating?
c: the strings, rubbed by the bow
items.e: All sounds are made by something vibrating.

items.q: A guitar string is tightened. What happens to the pitch?
items.e: Tighter strings vibrate faster.

items.q: Chloe likes to bang a pot with a spoon. What vibrates to make the sound?
items.e: The pot vibrates.

items.q: Hana's rubber band makes sound. What is it doing?
items.e: Sound comes from vibrating things.

items.q: Ava likes to snap a rubber band. What vibrates to make the sound?
items.e: The rubber band vibrates.

items.q: Ethan likes to clap. What vibrates to make the sound?
items.e: Your hands and the air vibrates.

items.q: Zoe taps the drum. The rice jumps. Why?
items.e: The drum shakes fast. That makes the rice jump.

items.q: When a tambourine makes a sound, what is vibrating?
c: the skin and the small metal discs
items.e: All sounds are made by something vibrating.

items.q: Sound travels best through which of these?
c: a solid like a wooden desk
items.e: Particles in solids are close together.

items.q: How does a hearing aid help a person?
c: It makes sounds louder so the person can hear them.
items.e: Technology can help people hear.

items.q: Zoe likes to strum a ukulele. What vibrates to make the sound?
items.e: The strings vibrates.

items.q: Maya sees the drum shake. What does it make?
items.e: Shaking makes sound.

items.q: Which sound is the loudest?
items.e: Loud sounds can damage hearing.

items.q: When your voice makes a sound, what is vibrating?
c: the player's lips and the air in the tube
items.e: All sounds are made by something vibrating.

items.q: Arjun sees the rubber band shake. What does it make?
items.e: Shaking makes sound.

items.q: “Tiny bones pass the vibrations to the inner ear.” What happened just before?
c: Nerves send a message to the brain, and we hear the sound.
Something vibrates and makes the air vibrate.
The vibrations travel through the air into the ear.
items.e: Vibration → air → eardrum → tiny bones → nerves → brain.

items.q: Can sound travel through a vacuum (with no air at all)?
c: No, there are no particles to carry the vibrations.
Yes, the vibrations can pass through it.
Only if it is very loud.
items.e: Sound needs a solid, liquid or gas to travel through.
